## Encoding

The values one serialize function can write, read and measure, each packed into exactly the bits it needs.

<!-- nova-work:encoding:start -->

| feature | done |
|---|:---:|
| one serialize function for write, read and measure | ✅ |
| raw bits, 1 to 64 at a time | ✅ |
| bool, u8, u16, u32 and u64 | ✅ |
| ranged 32 and 64 bit integers | ✅ |
| 128 bit integers, raw and ranged | ✅ |
| a min == max range costs zero bits | ✅ |
| f32 and f64 | ✅ |
| compressed floats | ✅ |
| precomputed compressed float entry points | ✅ |
| fixed point (Q formats) serialized exactly | ✅ |
| relative sequence numbers (int_relative) | ✅ |
| byte arrays and alignment | ✅ |
| UTF-8 strings and UTF-16 wide strings | ✅ |
| a conservative size estimate before writing | ✅ |
| buffers past 256 MB round trip | ✅ |
| complete | 100% |

[Source data](docs/roadmap.sexp)

<!-- nova-work:encoding:end -->

## Reading untrusted data

The read path is the trust boundary: hostile packet data is refused with an error, never a panic.

<!-- nova-work:untrusted:start -->

| feature | done |
|---|:---:|
| hostile data is refused, never panics | ✅ |
| out-of-range values in bit headroom refused | ✅ |
| a refused read leaves its destination unwritten | ✅ |
| failure is terminal until the stream is rebuilt | ✅ |
| malformed UTF-8 and UTF-16 refused | ✅ |
| int_relative results outside the int32 domain refused | ✅ |
| custom serialize functions refuse decoded values (stream.refuse) | ❌ |
| write and measure cannot fail (Infallible error type) | ✅ |
| no unsafe code, enforced by the compiler | ✅ |
| complete | 88% |

[Source data](docs/roadmap.sexp)

<!-- nova-work:untrusted:end -->
